references.text: The first day shall be a holy assembly, and the seventh day a holy assembly. No kind of work shall be done on these days, except for preparing food.
On the first day you shall hold a holy assembly. You shall not do any ordinary work. This is the parallel commandment concerning the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
On the first day there shall be a holy assembly, and you shall not do any ordinary work. The same principle regarding holy assemblies and prohibitions on work during festivals applies.
The Sabbath commandment that forbids work on holy days is the basis for the prohibition against work on festival days.
On the seventh day there shall be a festive assembly for the Lord your God. You shall not do any work. The same festival regulation appears in Deuteronomy.
On the first day of the seventh month you shall hold a holy assembly and not do ordinary work. The same wording is used for other festival days.
There remains therefore a Sabbath rest for the people of God. For whoever has entered his rest, has also rested from their works. The New Testament interprets the Sabbath rest spiritually.
